Users report wrong sums, maxima, and threshold-search results after mixing range
updates in production. The root cause is unknown. The visible test reproduces
one sequence, but other workloads also disagree with the stored values.

Investigate and repair `src/range-tree.js`. Preserve the CommonJS named export
`RangeTree` and the complete API documented in its source comment, including
half-open ranges, error handling, and empty-range behavior. Keep O(log n) updates
and queries, O(n) construction and `toArray()`, and O(n) storage; a rewrite that
scans the affected range is not acceptable. Do not add dependencies.

Work only in the current directory. Do not modify `test/` or `package.json`.
Verify the fix with `node --test`.

.
  - test/                           just now
    - range-tree.test.js  414B      22h ago
  - src/                            just now
    - range-tree.js       6.9KB     22h ago
  - package.json          119B      22h ago

Three defects in `src/range-tree.js`: assignment retains an obsolete addition tag, partial maximum queries start at `0`, and threshold search reads children before propagating lazy updates. I’ll fix those paths and add regression tests outside `test/`, preserving the API and tree complexity.

Fixed three independent defects in `src/range-tree.js`:

- Assignment now clears pending additions, preventing overwritten updates from resurfacing during propagation.
- Partial maximum queries use `-Infinity`, so negative-only ranges return the correct maximum.
- `firstAtLeast()` propagates lazy tags before searching children.

Preserved the CommonJS `RangeTree` export, documented API, and complexity bounds: O(log n) updates/queries and O(n) construction, `toArray()`, and storage.

Added `range-tree.regression.test.js` covering all three defects, deterministic mixed-update comparisons against an array oracle, and API edge cases. Left `test/` and `package.json` unchanged.

Verification: regressions reproduced the failures before the fix; **`node --test` passes all 6 tests** afterward.
